feedback: No earlier race exists, so this feedback rests only on the contract and on what the Integrator had to set for this geometry. Five sensors at 15 mm spacing span 0.06 m, which is 2.4 times the 25 mm tape. Sensor weights were scaled linearly with x so that the signal stays within ±1. This left kp at about 4, a moderate value, so the controller does not need extra gain to hold the line. If the next race shows line_loss_events on the sharpest bends, widen the sensor span toward the ±0.08 limit, because the outer sensors are what keep the line in view before it leaves the array. If steering_oscillation is high, the controller is over-gained for the sensor lead; reduce the lead by moving sensor y closer to the axle (for example 0.03 m) rather than adding derivative action, because the sensor lead sets how much lag the loop sees. If completion_time is too long and the run completes with no line loss, the geometry is not the limit; raise base_speed, not geometry. If rms_error is high but there is no oscillation or line loss, sensor footprints are probably too large for the 25 mm tape, so try sensor_size 0.008.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are above zero on the oval or s-bend, widen the sensor span to x = ±0.04 (five sensors at 0.02 spacing) to keep the outer sensors on the tape before the robot leaves it. Evidence: none yet; this is a contract-based prediction to test first.

If steering_oscillation is high in the next race, move sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 to reduce the lead the loop sees, keeping the other geometry fields fixed. Evidence: none yet; this is a contract-based prediction.
If rms_error is high with no line loss or oscillation, try sensor_size 0.008 to tighten the footprint on the 25 mm tape. Evidence: none yet; this is a contract-based prediction.
